description: CAPT-SPEC 2026-07-12 (v4.0.0) — partMass_g now comes from a DRAWING THAT EXISTS. Until today this recipe demanded SOLL 10.35 g with toleranceSource 'drawing', and there was no drawing: erp.articles.gewicht_kg was NULL for all 222 articles, qms.characteristics carried no injection-moulding characteristic at all, and the recipe itself admitted the bands 'mirror the housing-A SOLL' — an article that does not exist in the 222-article master. Meanwhile machine.ts drew part masses as normal(partMassTargetG, 0.8 %), zero-mean noise about the machine's own config constant, so the machine's true mean was exactly 10.40 g. The celebrated Ca of 0.147 was thus the distance between a sim constant and a typed number, wearing a provenance that pointed at nothing. --- WHAT IS TRUE NOW. The part sgm-004 actually runs is _V4_12-0044-003 ("Steckergehäuse Typ C"), and it already had a RELEASED drawing in the PLM (DWG-12-0044-003) whose content column was NULL. The place existed; it was empty. It now holds the geometry, and the band below is DERIVED from it: cavity volume 7.936 cm3 x 1.36 g/cm3 (PA66-GF30, ISO 1183) = 10.79 g nominal, and the limits [10.31, 11.27] are NOT a second typed number — they are the drawing's wall-thickness tolerance (2 +/- 0.1 mm) propagated through the same volume formula. Because the number now comes from the product's geometry, toleranceSource 'drawing' finally RESOLVES: windchill.documents -> DWG-12-0044-003. The band is BINDING and may not be widened to make a deviation vanish — widening it would mean re-drawing the part. --- THE MACHINE STILL DEVIATES, AND NOW FOR A REASON. The sim no longer carries a magic mass offset. It moulds the cavity (7.936 cm3) and the melt is PACKED: part mass rises with holding pressure, which is exactly why a setter weighs parts to dial Nachdruck in. sgm-004's mould is a USED tool, and the sim's own wear model already raises the pressure as a tool ages (wearPressureFactor, machine.ts) — so the machine packs above the design point and every part comes out ~0.9 % heavy. Small, physical, and invisible: 100 % of parts stay INSIDE the drawing band while the process centre is off. That is the product's whole claim, and it is now earned rather than staged. --- SEPARATION OF KINDS: partMass_g is a PRODUCT characteristic (drawing, binding). mouldTempC is a RESIN property (norm, binding). The pressures / hot-runner / cushion are MACHINE SETTINGS from the process data sheet (process_estimate, optimisable) and are passed through here untouched. Throwing all three into one file under one 'drawing' stamp is what produced the fiction we just removed. --- CAPT-REGIME 2026-07-29, TWO THINGS MEASURED ON THIS MACHINE THAT THIS FILE USED TO GET WRONG. (1) THE GATE. mouldTempC carried no `gate` here between 9d50b52 and today, and that was not a decision this file was able to make: the operative guard lives on profiles/machines/injection-molding-machine.json#recipe_mould_temp_band (`when: inCycle==true`), which is what it-evaluator copies into the spec and what edge-api turns into its interval CTE. `parameters[].gate` has no consumer at all. So the removal changed nothing except what this file CLAIMED, and the claim was false for 17 days. The guard is restored here as a mirror, and ci/lint-recipes.mjs now fails the build if the two ever disagree again. Keeping the guard is also the substantive answer: the profile's own measurement says an idle SGM reads exactly 25.00 degC ambient, so an ungated mouldTempC band would raise a deviation against a recipe that is not running. What CAPT-WINDOW believed would replace the gate — `population` excluding the cold data BY CONSTRUCTION — does not happen; see (2). (2) THE POPULATION IS DECLARED AND DORMANT. Every band above declares scope current_regime with on_change [mouldId, resin]. Measured over the full retained history on the live edge (7 d, 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-29): mouldId changed 0 times, resin changed 0 times. The edge honours the declaration and answers `regime_start: null` — 'NO declared marker has ever fired' — so the population IS the full history, and the live Golden answers are computed over all 599,522 hotrunnerTempC and 11,842 partMass_g samples. The declaration is CORRECT and it is signed; it is simply not yet doing any narrowing, and it will not until this machine is re-tooled or re-materialled. It is left exactly as it is: the alternative marker that does move, currentProgram (1,871 changes in the same 7 days), is a job number and not a process regime — declaring it would drop partMass_g to 23 samples, under min_sample_n 1000, and trade two working verdicts for two evidence gaps. --- 2026-07-31 WAVE-3, hotrunnerTempC SOLL 230 -> 295 degC. The 230 in this file was never this machine's setpoint. sgm-004 is an Engel victory 120 running PA66-GF30 and its configured nozzle setpoint IS 295 degC (sim-v5 packages/machines-sgm/src/config.ts:337 — barrelSetpointsC [270,282,290,295], nozzleSetpointC 295); the simulator DERIVES the resin FROM that setpoint (resinForNozzleTemp(), config.ts:257-261: >=268 -> PA66) and couples it to the part-mass model, so 295 is the intended truth and lowering the machine to meet this band would corrupt the simulation. hotrunnerTempC is published per cavity as nozzleC + normal(0, 1.5) (machine.ts:1281-1283), i.e. N(295, 1.5^2) in steady state. MEASURED by the consumer 2026-07-31: mean 295.0, range 289.9-300.5 over 6277 samples in 2 h — a textbook fit to N(295,1.5) at +-3.7 sigma, and 65 degC above the 230 this file used to demand, so EVERY judgement on this signal was against a number nobody aims for. Both bands are re-centred on 295 with their EXISTING half-widths PRESERVED: the temp band keeps +-6.5 -> [288.5,301.5] (+-4.33 sigma, Cp = 13/(6*1.5) = 1.44 >= cp_min 1.33, and it contains the measured range with margin), the control limits keep warn +-3.5 / action +-4.5 about SOLL-0.5 -> warn [291,298], action [290,299] (action = 3 sigma, which is what an Eingriffsgrenze is supposed to be). NO width was widened to buy silence — only the centre moved, and the centre is the machine spec. Temp-band upper 301.5 and action upper 299 both stay inside the equipment envelope [180,310] raised in the same wave (equipment_hotrunner_temp_envelope). toleranceSource stays 'process_estimate': this is a machine setting off the process data sheet, not a drawing number. --- 2026-09-20 WELLE-A / CAPT-REZEPT: THE ESCALATION GEOMETRY WAS INSIDE OUT. MEASURED on this file before the change: the ACTION tier lay INSIDE the tolerance it is supposed to protect (action [290,299] inside tolerance [288.5,301.5]). Read together with the consumer's contract that is the wrong way round: brain-operator treats WARN as 'keep running, correct' and ACTION as 'stop the machine' (sim-v5 packages/brain-operator/src/decide.ts + deterministic-stop.ts), so the old numbers ordered a STOP at 289.5 degC — a value at which the part is still inside its own band and the press is still making good parts. THE RULE APPLIED HERE, to every tier in this file: (1) ACTION IS THE TOLERANCE LIMIT ITSELF. An Eingriffsgrenze that stops the line may not fire while the part is in spec, and it may not wait until scrap has been running for a while either — so it is not a second number, it IS the spec limit. (2) WARN IS THE TOLERANCE NARROWED BY 2 SIGMA of the signal's own measured scatter: the Warngrenze belongs where the process's ordinary 95 % spread first reaches the tolerance limit, because past that point noise alone starts producing out-of-spec parts and that is precisely when a setter must correct while the part is still good. Nesting is therefore warn subset tolerance = action, proven per machine in the PR's table, and no width was widened to buy silence — the only reason a limit moved outward is that it had been standing inside the spec. APPLIED TO THIS MACHINE: MEASURED hotrunnerTempC (host .120, 2026-09-20, SgmMachine over the shipped DEFAULT_CONFIG, 3 h at 1 Hz, first 15 min discarded) n = 79,200, mean 294.995, sd 1.5008, range [288.9, 301.4] — a textbook fit to the generator machine.ts:1834 `nozzleC + normal(0, 1.5)` and to the 2026-07-31 live measurement this file already records. 2 sigma = 3.0 degC, so warn = [291.5, 298.5] and action = [288.5, 301.5]. The old warn [291,298] was not symmetric about the SOLL at all: it preserved a historical '+-3.5 / -4.5 about SOLL-0.5' offset, giving a 4.0 degC reserve below and 3.0 above the same nominal. Same rule on both sides now. Nesting: warn [291.5,298.5] subset tolerance = action [288.5,301.5] subset equipment envelope [180,310] (equipment_hotrunner_temp_envelope). Noise behaviour, from the same sample: the warn half-width 3.5 degC is 2.33 sigma (1.98 % of individual samples, removed as chatter by the rule's 2-of-3 persistence), the action half-width 6.5 degC is 4.33 sigma and exactly ONE of 79,200 samples touched it — so ACTION does not fire on noise. It does fire on every injected setpoint drift: the drift step is 8-15 degC (machine.ts DRIFT_MAGNITUDE_MIN_C/MAX_C) and even the smallest step exceeds the 6.5 degC action half-width, so no drift on this axis can hide inside the band. --- 2026-09-20 WELLE-A / CAPT-REZEPT: mouldTempC GETS CONTROL LIMITS, AND THE HALF-TRUTH ABOUT WHY IT HAD NONE. It is not that nothing judged mouldTempC: profiles/machines/injection-molding-machine.json declares `mould_temp_control_limits` (op within_limits, deviation_class recipe) with a LITERAL warn [82,88] / action [78,92]. The defect is that the literal is ONE global band for every injection-moulding machine in the fleet — the exact construction CAPT-STURM measured on hotrunner_control_limits on 2026-07-12 ('a control limit is meaningless without the setpoint it is centred on') and wave-3 retired on 2026-07-31 by moving that rule onto `valueFrom`. mouldTempC was left behind, so no RECIPE carried a warn/action split for it and every consumer that reads recipes rather than the baked profile was blind to it. This file now supplies the band. NO PROFILE EDIT IS NEEDED FOR IT TO BE READ: the it-evaluator's RecipeBandResolver derives a recipe-class constraint's ref as `c.require?.valueFrom ?? refByConstraint.get(cid) ?? recipe:<cid>` (recipe-band-resolver.ts, indexProfiles), and `mould_temp_control_limits` resolves through the third arm to exactly `recipe:mould_temp_control_limits`. GEOMETRY, same rule as above: action := the tolerance band [80,90] verbatim (the PA-resin norm, untouched); warn := narrowed by 2 sigma. MEASURED (host .120, 2026-09-20, SgmMachine driven over the shipped DEFAULT_CONFIG, 3 h at 1 Hz, first 15 min discarded): mouldTempC n = 9,900, mean 87.51, sd 0.795 — the generator is machines-sgm/src/machine.ts:1895 `mouldTempC + normal(0, MOULD_TEMP_SIGMA_C)` with MOULD_TEMP_SIGMA_C = 0.8. 2 sigma = 1.6 degC gives [81.6, 88.4]; published as [82, 88], i.e. TIGHTER than the rule demands. Two reasons, both deliberate: tighter is the safe direction for a warn tier, and [82,88] is byte-identical to the literal the EDGE OT detector still evaluates (the edge is literals-only and ignores valueFrom), so while that literal stands the central recipe-driven verdict and the edge verdict cannot contradict each other on this signal. WHAT IT CHANGES, MEASURED: a mouldSetpointC drift event (machine.ts injectSetpointDrift, one step of 8-15 degC, DRIFT_MAGNITUDE_MIN_C/MAX_C) moves the TCU target from 87.5 to 95.5-102.5 degC. In a run on this host sgm-005's target drifted +11.4 degC to 98.9 and mouldTempC settled at mean 98.52 / p99 100.8 — an ACTION excursion against [80,90], and previously an excursion with nothing in ANY recipe to escalate against. brain-operator states the gap in its own source: MONITORED_PARAMS holds a single entry because 'of the SGM parameters, only hotrunnerTempC has a warn/action split in any live recipe ... It is still ONE entry, and that is a DATA gap, not a code gap' (decide.ts). This closes that data gap; wiring the second entry is Welle B. THE HONEST CONSEQUENCE, STATED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED IN PRODUCTION: the TCU aims at 87.5 degC (MOULD_TCU_TARGET_C) while this recipe's SOLL is 85 — the deliberate, documented 2.5 degC off-centre process (Ca = 2.5/5 = 0.50, four times the ca_max 0.125 this very file demands). 87.5 sits only 0.62 sigma under the warn upper limit, so WARN will be breached on roughly a quarter of all samples and, through the rule's 2-of-3 persistence, will stand essentially permanently. That is not a false alarm and the cure is not a wider band: it is the same verdict the capability rule already renders, finally visible on the tier a setter reads. ACTION stays clean — 90 degC is 3.1 sigma above the process centre and was not reached in 9,900 samples — so a standing WARN can never turn into a stop. --- 2026-09-20 WELLE-A / CAPT-REZEPT, A MEASUREMENT HANDED ON RATHER THAN A CHANGE MADE. The HOLD-gated pressure plateau is exactly derivable from the machine constant: during HOLD the sim drives currentPressureBar to holdBar = injectionPressureBar x wearPressureFactor x 0.5 and reports peakPressureBar = that x 1.05, holdPressureBar = that x 0.7 (machine.ts:1120-1155, :1868-1870). Measured over one cycle on this host, sgm-004 (injectionPressureBar 1000, mould life 100 %): peak 525 bar and hold 350 bar on the plateau, preceded by ONE ramp-in sample at 483 / 322 bar that the `phaseName==HOLD` gate lets into the population. Both plateau values sit inside this file's bands, so nothing is broken today — but wearPressureFactor = 1 + (100 - lifePercent) x 0.003 lifts the plateau by up to +30 % over the tool's life, and 525 x 1.0667 = 560 is this band's own upper limit: below about 78 % mould life sgm-004's peak pressure leaves recipe:peak_pressure_band and never comes back. The band is deliberately NOT widened here — widening a band so a real, physical drift stops being reported is the comfortable lie this file spent four versions removing. The honest repair is a wear-aware band or a plateau-only gate, and both live in profiles/. Recorded so the next wave inherits the measurement instead of the surprise. --- 2026-09-20 WELLE-A / CAPT-REZEPT, WHAT THIS FILE STILL DOES NOT HAVE, AND WHY IT IS NOT IN THIS COMMIT. partMass_g, cushionMm, peakPressureBar and holdPressureBar carry a band but NO control limits, and a recipe alone cannot give them one: a control limit only reaches the engine through a PROFILE constraint with op within_limits and deviation_class recipe, and profiles/machines/injection-molding-machine.json declares exactly two of those (hotrunner_control_limits, mould_temp_control_limits). The resolver asks the recipe only for the refs its own constraints name (recipe-band-resolver.ts indexProfiles -> resolveFromBindings), so a `recipe:part_mass_control_limits` key written here would be requested by nobody: dead data that READS like coverage, which is worse than the gap it hides. The missing constraints are a profiles/ change and belong to the wave that may touch profiles/. Same reason no parameter was added for the ~50 further values the machine publishes (barrel zone setpoints, nozzleSetpointC, mouldSetpointC, injectionSpeedMmPerSec, backPressureBar, shotVolumeCm3, coolingFlowLMin, cycleTimeSec, cavityPressureBar, mouldPressureBar): none of them has a recipe-class constraint, and the three setpoint axes are not even in the profile's 48-attribute vocabulary, so a band on them would be invisible to the engine and to the UI. --- CAPT-LEAD 2026-09-20, five more parameters. A real injection-moulding recipe carries more than seven entries, and the ceiling was never this file - it was the profile: RecipeBandResolver only asks for refs that a deviation_class 'recipe' constraint names. SMProfile-InjectionMoldingMachine 2.4.0 adds five, and here are the bands. Every number is read out of machines-sgm, not estimated: melt temperature nozzleTempC follows activeNozzleSetpointC at 0.5 degC/tick with no noise (machine.ts), so soll IS the setpoint and the band mirrors the hot-runner tolerance of the same machine. injectionSpeedMmPerSec is jitter(60, 0.05) and backPressureBar is jitter(100, 0.10), and jitter(c, r) = c * (1 +- r) UNIFORM, so sigma = c*r/sqrt(3); the bands are mean +- 4 sigma, which is Cp = 1.33 at Ca = 0 - the back-pressure band is wide because the simulated jitter is wide, and narrowing it would manufacture a permanent capability finding out of nothing. coolingFlowLMin is a constant 22.0 L/min while RUNNING and 0 otherwise, hence the +-10 % band and the inCycle gate: 0 against a band is a category error, not a finding. cycleTimeSec is cfg.cycleTimeSec unless an assignment overrides it, +-10 %. DELIBERATELY ABSENT: shotVolumeCm3. machine.ts computes it as cavities * partMassTargetG / 1.1 when the mould has no design record, and its own comment calls that 'the causality of injection moulding exactly upside down' - a value the source flags as wrong gets no band. See audits/2026-09-20/ in the sim-v5 repo.
